name: Approve an account
statement: The system shall let an administrator approve a pending account so that the person can sign in.
notes: Needs an Account object in the ontology. A new account starts pending. Approval is a status change in Playground only: Keycloak is not called (decision 24).

name: A pending account sees only its status
statement: The system shall let a person with a pending account see only that their account is waiting for approval, and refuse everything else.
notes: The person can sign in at Keycloak and gets a token, but our API refuses every request except asking for their own status (decision 24). It replaced 'prevent from signing in'.

name: Deactivate an account
statement: The system shall let an administrator deactivate an account, with a reason.
notes: An administrator cannot deactivate themselves: a rule to write in the ontology. The reason and the audit entry are kept by Playground. The backend disables the person in Keycloak and ends their sessions (decision 23).

name: Reinstate an account
statement: The system shall let an administrator reinstate a deactivated account.
notes: The backend enables the person in Keycloak again and sets the account active (decisions 23 and 24).

name: One account role
statement: The system shall give each account exactly one role: member, administrator or auditor.
notes: The account role is kept in Playground's database, not in Keycloak (decision 23, amended). Project roles stay in our database too.

name: Sign in through single sign-on
statement: The system shall let a person sign in through single sign-on.
notes: Keycloak configuration. Single sign-on proves who the person is and nothing else: roles stay in Playground, and a person with no account is refused and offered the account request page. The release is the owner's call.

name: Access is checked on the server
statement: The system shall check access on the server for every command and read.
stimulus: A person asks for something their role does not allow.
environment: Normal operation, with the browser's role switch off.
measure: An acceptance test for each role shows a refusal on every command and every read.
sources: release plan R1; risk register R-08; north star
notes: The server checks the Keycloak token (signature, expiry, issuer) on every request, then checks project membership (decision 23).

name: A new person arrives pending
statement: The system shall create a pending account the first time a person it does not know reaches it through the identity provider.
notes: Our API holds the person until an administrator approves. Needs the Account object in the ontology.

name: Sign in through the identity provider
statement: The system shall let a person sign in through the identity provider.
notes: Keycloak does it. Our side: send the person there, then check the token that comes back.

name: Sign out
statement: The system shall let a person sign out.
notes: Keycloak ends its session. We clear our own session.

name: Show name and account role
statement: The system shall show a signed-in person their name and account role.
notes: The name comes from the token and the role from our account. Passwords and email are changed on Keycloak's own account page.

name: Refuse a request with no valid token
statement: The system shall refuse a request that has no valid token from the identity provider.
notes: A valid token has the right signature, has not expired, and was issued by the identity provider for this product.

name: No role change from our screens
statement: The system shall not let anyone give or take away an account role from its own screens.
notes: A role is changed in Keycloak only, so a hacked administrator session cannot make a second administrator.
